newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen seen higher after weak data.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen seen higher after weak data.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures gained ground on Tuesday after the release of weaker than expected machinery orders data dampened expectations of an impending Japanese rate hike.
Japan's core private machinery orders for April rose 7.2 percent month-on-month, against market forecasts of a 14 percent rise.
"Sentiment is not as strong as it was two weeks ago where people were so sure they were going to hike rates," a dealer at a European bank said.
He said the lead December Euroyen contract showed scope to climb to 99.00 or 99.05 but was unlikely to head much beyond that before the Bank of Japan's quarterly business sentiment survey on June 25.
December Euroyen stood at 98.95 at 1115 GMT against its IMM close at 98.94. It fell to an early low of 98.93 following strong gains in Tokyo stocks.
September JGBs ended at 123.23 against a previous 123.25.
Eurodollar futures ended little changed in a featureless session with no key U.S. data due until later in the week.

The bank dealer said December Eurodollars were likely to trade on the higher end of a 93.75-93.85 range after the release of relatively subdued U.S. employment data last week reduced the likelihood of an interest rate hike.
December Eurodollars ended unchanged against their IMM close at 93.820 on volume of 4,850 lots.
